llm/vibevoice.tagline: Open voice AI for long multi-speaker audio
llm/vibevoice.overview: VibeVoice is Microsoft's open-weights speech model that turns written scripts into long-form spoken audio with several distinct speakers, making it well-suited for podcasts, audiobooks, and dialogue. The project also ships VibeVoice-ASR, a companion speech-to-text model that transcribes up to 60 minutes of audio in one pass with speaker labels and timestamps. Because the weights are open, you can run it yourself instead of paying a per-character TTS API.
capabilities: Generates long-form, multi-speaker spoken audio from a single text script
Keeps separate, consistent voices for each named speaker in a conversation
Includes VibeVoice-ASR for transcription with Who / When / What output
ASR is multilingual across 50+ languages and handles 60-minute clips in one pass
Integrates with Hugging Face Transformers and supports faster vLLM inference
useCases: Creators producing a two-host podcast from a written script without recording
Students turning study notes or articles into narrated audio to listen on the go
Anyone needing accurate, speaker-labeled transcripts of long meetings or lectures
howTo: Open the official Colab notebook from the repo to try streaming TTS with zero local setup
For local use, clone github.com/microsoft/VibeVoice and install its Python requirements
Download the model weights from the Hugging Face VibeVoice collection
Write a script that labels each line by speaker, then run the demo to synthesize the audio
For transcription, load microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR through Hugging Face Transformers

example.label: Multi-speaker script format
example.content:
Speaker 1: Welcome back to the show.
Speaker 2: Thanks for having me, glad to be here.

goodToKnow: Generation runs best on a GPU; long multi-speaker clips are heavy to produce on CPU only.
It is a research release, so check Microsoft's license and responsible-use notes before publishing voices.

llm/kronos-2.tagline: Open foundation model for financial candlesticks
llm/kronos-2.overview: Kronos is an open-weights 499M-parameter foundation model built specifically to forecast financial time series like candlestick (K-line) price data. It was pre-trained on data from over 45 global exchanges, so it understands the patterns of open, high, low, close, and volume sequences. You feed it recent market history and it predicts the likely next candles.
capabilities: Forecasts future candlestick (OHLCV) sequences from recent market history
Pre-trained across 45+ global exchanges for broad market coverage
Comes in several sizes via the NeoQuasar Hugging Face collection
Ships fine-tuning scripts to adapt the model to your own instrument or task
Provides a simple predictor wrapper for plugging in your own price data
useCases: Students learning quantitative finance who want a real model to experiment with
Researchers benchmarking time-series forecasting on market data
Builders prototyping a price-trend signal before committing to a full strategy
howTo: Clone github.com/shiyu-coder/Kronos and install the Python dependencies
Download a checkpoint such as NeoQuasar/Kronos-small from Hugging Face
Load the tokenizer and model, then wrap them with the provided KronosPredictor
Pass a dataframe of recent OHLCV history and call predict for the forecast horizon
Optionally run the fine-tuning scripts to specialize it on your own dataset

example.label: Generate a forecast
example.content:
predictor = KronosPredictor(model, tokenizer)
preds = predictor.predict(df=recent_klines, pred_len=24)

goodToKnow: Forecasts are statistical estimates, not financial advice; never trade real money on raw model output.
Accuracy depends heavily on clean, correctly formatted OHLCV input at a consistent interval.

llm/wan2-1.tagline: Open video generation that runs on consumer GPUs
llm/wan2-1.overview: Wan2.1 is Wan-Video's open suite of video foundation models, with a flagship 14B version and a lighter 1.3B version that needs only about 8 GB of VRAM. It generates video and images from text or image prompts and also handles image-to-video, video editing, and text-to-image. It is notable for being able to render readable Chinese and English text inside generated video.
capabilities: Generates video from text prompts or animates a still image into motion
Runs the 1.3B model on consumer GPUs (about 8 GB VRAM, ~4 min for 5s 480p on an RTX 4090)
Supports multiple tasks: text-to-video, image-to-video, editing, and text-to-image
Can render legible English and Chinese text inside generated frames
Includes an efficient Wan-VAE for encoding and decoding longer, higher-res clips
useCases: Creators making short social clips or B-roll from a text description
Students experimenting with open video generation without renting a cloud GPU
Designers animating a product still into a short looping motion piece
howTo: Clone github.com/Wan-Video/Wan2.1 and install the listed requirements
Download the matching weights from the Wan-AI Hugging Face organization
Pick a size: the 1.3B model for consumer GPUs or 14B for higher quality
Run the generation script with your text or image prompt and target resolution
Find the rendered MP4 in the output folder and iterate on the prompt

example.label: Text-to-video command
example.content: python generate.py --task t2v-1.3B --size 480p --prompt "a fox running through autumn leaves, cinematic"

goodToKnow: The 14B model is much higher quality but needs far more VRAM than the 1.3B version.
Generation time grows quickly with resolution and clip length, so start short and small.

llm/unlimited-ocr.tagline: Open OCR for long, multi-page documents
llm/unlimited-ocr.overview: Unlimited OCR Works is Baidu's open-weights OCR model that extracts text from images and documents, built specifically to handle long or multi-page inputs in a single pass. It pushes the DeepSeek-OCR approach further toward what Baidu calls one-shot long-horizon parsing. You point it at a scan, PDF page, or image and it returns the recognized text.
capabilities: Extracts text from images, scans, and PDF pages
Designed for long-horizon, multi-page documents rather than single crops
Runs through Hugging Face Transformers with trust_remote_code
Supports faster serving via vLLM for higher throughput
Open weights available on Hugging Face and ModelScope
useCases: Students digitizing lecture notes, textbooks, or handwritten scans into text
Anyone converting long PDFs or reports into searchable, copyable text
Developers building a document-ingestion pipeline that needs free, local OCR
howTo: Install the tested dependencies (torch, transformers, Pillow, pymupdf, einops, etc.)
Load baidu/Unlimited-OCR with AutoModel and AutoTokenizer using trust_remote_code=True
Pass your image or PDF page to the model to get recognized text back
For large workloads, serve the model with vLLM for faster batch inference
Alternatively, try the model first in the Hugging Face Spaces demo

example.label: Load the model
example.content:
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained('baidu/Unlimited-OCR', trust_remote_code=True)

goodToKnow: Requirements are tested on an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA, so a capable GPU is expected for good speed.
OCR accuracy varies with scan quality; very faint or skewed pages may still need cleanup.

llm/z-image-turbo.overview: Z-Image is Alibaba (Tongyi-MAI)'s open-weights image generation family with 6B parameters, and Z-Image-Turbo is the distilled variant tuned for fast generation. It uses a single-stream diffusion transformer to turn text prompts into images quickly. Open checkpoints are on Hugging Face and ModelScope, with online demos to try first.
capabilities: Generates images from text prompts using a 6B single-stream diffusion transformer
Turbo variant is distilled for noticeably faster generation
Open checkpoints available on both Hugging Face and ModelScope
Hosted online demos let you test prompts before installing anything
Part of a family that includes a higher-quality non-turbo base model
useCases: Designers and students iterating on visual concepts quickly and cheaply
Builders adding local, free image generation to an app or workflow
Anyone who wants fast previews without a slow many-step diffusion run
howTo: Try Z-Image-Turbo first in the Hugging Face Spaces online demo
To run locally, clone github.com/Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image and install its requirements
Download the Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo checkpoint from Hugging Face
Run the provided inference script with your text prompt
Adjust the prompt and seed, then re-run to explore variations

example.label: Sample prompt
example.content: "a cozy reading nook by a rain-streaked window, warm lamp light, soft focus, photographic"

goodToKnow: Turbo trades a little fidelity for speed; use the full Z-Image base model when quality matters most.
A GPU is recommended for comfortable local generation speeds.

llm/ace-step-1-5.tagline: Open 4B model that generates full music tracks
llm/ace-step-1-5.overview: ACE-Step 1.5 is ACE Music's open-weights 4B model that generates complete music tracks from text prompts describing genre, mood, and instruments. You can run it locally on a GPU or, if you have no GPU, use the free hosted version at acemusic.ai. It offers a CLI, a Python API, a REST API, and a Gradio web UI, plus LoRA training to fine-tune your own style.
capabilities: Generates full-length music tracks from a text description
Offers multiple interfaces: CLI wizard, Python API, REST API, and Gradio UI
Runs on CUDA GPUs with fallback support for MPS, ROCm, Intel XPU, and CPU
Supports LoRA training to teach it your own musical style
Free hosted option at acemusic.ai for users without a GPU
useCases: Creators needing royalty-free background music for videos or reels
Students exploring AI music generation without buying studio software
Developers adding a music-generation feature through the REST or Python API
howTo: If you have no GPU, just use the free hosted app at acemusic.ai
To run locally, install uv, then clone github.com/ACE-Step/ACE-Step-1.5
Run uv sync inside the folder to install dependencies (Python 3.11-3.12)
Launch the Gradio UI or CLI wizard and enter a text prompt for your track
Optionally follow the LoRA training guide to fine-tune your own sound

example.label: Local setup
example.content:
git clone https://github.com/ACE-Step/ACE-Step-1.5.git
cd ACE-Step-1.5
uv sync

goodToKnow: A CUDA GPU is recommended; CPU generation works but is slow.
Always check the license and any usage terms before publishing or monetizing generated music.

llm/gencad.tagline: Generate editable CAD geometry with AI
llm/gencad.overview: GenCAD is an open-weights generative model that produces CAD designs, turning inputs such as sketch images into editable 3D engineering geometry rather than flat pictures. It is a research project combining an autoencoder, a contrastive image-CAD model (CCIP), and a diffusion prior. You can train its components or run inference to generate CAD from images.
capabilities: Generates editable parametric CAD geometry instead of static 3D meshes
Turns sketch or image inputs into engineering designs via a CCIP image-CAD model
Provides separate training stages for the autoencoder, CCIP, and diffusion prior
Includes inference scripts and a helper to convert STL files into images
Supports Docker and headless (xvfb) execution for server use
useCases: Engineering students experimenting with generative design from sketches
Researchers studying how generative models can produce editable CAD
Designers prototyping mechanical shapes before refining them in CAD software
howTo: Clone github.com/ferdous-alam/GenCAD and install requirements (or use the Docker image)
Download the provided model checkpoints into the expected model/ckpt folder
For headless servers, wrap inference with xvfb-run to enable visualization
Run inference_gencad.py, pointing it at your input image folder
Use stl2img.py if you need to prepare image inputs from existing STL files

example.label: Headless inference
example.content: xvfb-run python inference_gencad.py -image_path data/images -export_img

goodToKnow: This is a research codebase, so setup involves training stages and checkpoints rather than a one-line install.
Visualization needs a display or xvfb; on a plain server you must run it headless.

llm/hy-world-2-0.overview: HY-World 2.0 is Tencent Hunyuan's open-weights model that generates interactive 3D worlds and scenes from prompts or images, producing real 3D assets rather than just a video clip. Unlike video world models, its output is a persistent scene you can render in real time on a consumer GPU and import into engines like Blender, Unreal, or Isaac. A companion model can even reconstruct a 3D world from a casual video.
capabilities: Generates interactive, persistent 3D worlds and scenes from prompts or images
Outputs assets importable into Blender, Unreal Engine, and Isaac
Renders in real time on consumer GPUs after a one-time generation
Includes WorldMirror 2.0 to reconstruct 3D scenes from multi-view images or video
Supports panoramic world generation via the HY-Pano component
useCases: Game and XR developers prototyping explorable environments quickly
Students learning 3D world generation and digital-twin reconstruction
Creators turning a captured video into a reusable 3D scene
howTo: Clone github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HY-World-2.0 and install its inference dependencies
Download the open-sourced World Generation weights (WorldStereo 2.0 and related)
Run the world-generation inference script with a text prompt or input image
Export the generated scene and import it into Blender or Unreal Engine
To reconstruct from footage, use the WorldMirror 2.0 model on your video frames

example.label: Prompt idea
example.content: "a sunlit medieval courtyard with cobblestones, a fountain, and stone archways"

goodToKnow: World generation is GPU-heavy; rendering the finished scene is cheap, but creating it is not.
Different capabilities (world gen, panorama, reconstruction) use separate weights and code paths.

llm/void-video-object-and-interaction-de.tagline: Erase objects and their shadows from video
llm/void-video-object-and-interaction-de.overview: VOID is Netflix's open-weights 5B video-to-video model that removes objects from footage along with their interactions like shadows, reflections, and occlusions, so the cleanup looks natural. It uses two transformer passes you can chain for higher temporal consistency. The fastest way to try it is the included Colab notebook, which downloads the models and runs on a sample clip.
capabilities: Removes target objects from video, not just from single frames
Also cleans up related artifacts like shadows, reflections, and occlusions
Uses two sequential transformer passes for stronger temporal consistency
Builds its masks with SAM2/SAM3 and a Gemini-assisted pipeline stage
Ships a ready-to-run Colab notebook plus sample sequences
useCases: Video editors removing an unwanted person or object from a shot
Creators cleaning up footage without frame-by-frame manual rotoscoping
Researchers studying interaction-aware video inpainting
howTo: Open the VOID Colab notebook from the repo for the fastest no-setup trial
For local use, clone github.com/netflix/void-model and pip install requirements
Install SAM2 and SAM3 and set a Google AI API key for the masking stage
Download the base inpainting model (CogVideoX-Fun-V1.5-5b-InP) to the repo root
Run the inference script on your clip, optionally chaining both passes

example.label: Quick start
example.content: # Easiest path: open notebook.ipynb in Colab — it downloads models and runs a sample

goodToKnow: The mask pipeline's Stage 1 calls Gemini via the Google AI API, so you need an API key for that step.
It is a 5B model with several dependencies (SAM2/SAM3, ffmpeg), so expect a non-trivial GPU setup locally.

llm/lance.tagline: Open 3B model for text and images
llm/lance.overview: Lance is ByteDance's open-weights 3B multimodal model that handles both text and images, meaning it can read an image and answer questions or follow instructions about it alongside text input. At 3B parameters it is small enough to be relatively practical to run while still covering vision-language tasks. Weights and code are available openly via the project page and GitHub.
capabilities: Accepts both text and images as input in a single model
Answers questions and follows instructions grounded in an image
Compact 3B size keeps it lighter than large multimodal models
Open weights and code released by ByteDance
Suitable as a base for fine-tuning on multimodal tasks
useCases: Students building a simple visual question-answering demo
Developers adding lightweight image understanding to an app
Researchers needing a small open multimodal baseline to experiment with
howTo: Visit the project page at lance-project.github.io for model details and links
Clone github.com/bytedance/Lance and install its Python dependencies
Download the open weights as instructed in the repo
Load the model and pass an image plus a text question to run inference
Iterate on prompts, or fine-tune on your own multimodal data if needed

example.label: Multimodal prompt
example.content: image + "What objects are on the desk, and what is the person doing?"

goodToKnow: As a 3B model it is efficient but less capable than larger frontier multimodal models.
Check the repo for the exact supported input formats and any preprocessing steps.

llm/kandinsky-5.0-t2v-lite.overview: Kandinsky 5.0 T2V Lite is Kandinsky's open-weight text-to-video model, the lighter variant that generates short clips from text prompts. It is engineered to run on more modest hardware, with optimizations that let 5-second generation work on GPUs with as little as 12 GB of memory. It also supports image-to-video and camera-control LoRAs.
capabilities: Generates short video clips from text prompts
Lite variant optimized to run on GPUs with around 12 GB of VRAM
Supports image-to-video in addition to text-to-video
Selectable attention backends (Flash Attention, Sage Attention, or SDPA)
Camera-control LoRAs available for directing motion
useCases: Creators making quick short clips on a single consumer GPU
Students learning text-to-video without high-end hardware
Builders prototyping motion ideas before moving to a heavier model
howTo: Clone github.com/kandinskylab/kandinsky-5 and install the requirements
Download the Kandinsky 5.0 Video Lite weights as the README directs
Pick an attention engine with --attention_engine to fit your GPU
Run the text-to-video example with your prompt to render a 5-second clip
Try the inference example notebooks for image-to-video or camera LoRAs

example.label: Prompt idea
example.content: "a paper boat drifting down a rain puddle, soft reflections, slow motion"

goodToKnow: The first run is slower because of compilation; later runs hit the quoted latency.
Lite is faster and lighter but lower quality than the Pro variant.

llm/kandinsky-5.0-t2v-pro.overview: Kandinsky 5.0 T2V Pro is the higher-quality variant of Kandinsky's open-weight text-to-video family, generating better-looking clips from text prompts at the cost of heavier compute. It shares the same codebase as the Lite version and adds both text-to-video and image-to-video, plus camera-control LoRAs for guiding motion. Latency benchmarks were measured on an 80 GB H100 GPU.
capabilities: Generates higher-fidelity video clips from text prompts
Supports both text-to-video and image-to-video generation
Camera-control LoRAs available to direct shot motion
Selectable attention backends for performance tuning
Shares one repo and workflow with the Lite variant
useCases: Creators who want the best open text-to-video quality and have a strong GPU
Studios prototyping polished short clips before a full production render
Researchers comparing Pro vs Lite quality and speed trade-offs
howTo: Clone github.com/kandinskylab/kandinsky-5 and install the requirements
Download the Kandinsky 5.0 Video Pro weights as the README directs
Choose an attention engine suited to your GPU memory
Run the Pro text-to-video example with your prompt
Use the provided LoRAs or notebooks for camera control and image-to-video

example.label: Prompt idea
example.content: "aerial shot gliding over a misty mountain valley at sunrise, cinematic, 4k"

goodToKnow: Pro is significantly more demanding; benchmarks used an 80 GB H100, so plan for a high-VRAM GPU.
The first inference run is slower due to compilation before reaching steady-state latency.

llm/qwen-agentworld-35b-a3b.tagline: Open agent model that plans and calls tools
llm/qwen-agentworld-35b-a3b.overview: Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B is Qwen's open-weights language model with a mixture-of-experts design: 35B total parameters but only about 3B active per token, keeping it efficient. It is tuned for agent tasks that plan across multiple steps and call tools, making it a fit for building autonomous assistants. It serves through standard engines like vLLM and SGLang with an OpenAI-compatible API.
capabilities: Plans multi-step tasks and calls tools to complete them
Mixture-of-experts: 35B total but ~3B active per token for efficiency
Served via vLLM or SGLang with an OpenAI-compatible API
Usable directly through Hugging Face Transformers
Downloadable from Hugging Face or ModelScope
useCases: Developers building a tool-using agent that runs locally instead of via a paid API
Students learning how agentic LLMs plan and invoke tools
Teams wanting an open model for multi-step automation workflows
howTo: Download Qwen/Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B from Hugging Face (or ModelScope)
Serve it with vLLM or SGLang to get an OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Point your client at the local endpoint using the openai Python package
Send chat requests with tool definitions so the model can call them
For quick tests, load it directly with Transformers' AutoModelForCausalLM

example.label: Serve with vLLM
example.content: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 4

goodToKnow: Even with 3B active params, the full 35B weights need substantial GPU memory to serve.
Use vLLM or SGLang for practical speed; plain Transformers is fine only for small tests.

llm/dramabox-tts.tagline: Expressive open text-to-speech with voice cloning
llm/dramabox-tts.overview: Dramabox is Resemble AI's open-weights 3.3B text-to-speech model that turns written text into natural, expressive spoken audio, and it can match a reference voice sample. You can describe the delivery in the prompt (for example, warm or excited) and it follows that emotion. Every output is automatically watermarked with Resemble's imperceptible Perth watermark for traceability.
capabilities: Generates natural, emotionally expressive speech from text
Clones a target voice from a short reference audio sample
Lets you steer tone and emotion directly in the prompt text
Auto-watermarks output with the Perth neural watermark (can be disabled for debugging)
Offers a warm-server mode for faster repeated generation
useCases: Creators voicing characters or narration with a specific emotional tone
Developers adding expressive TTS to an app without a per-use API fee
Students experimenting with voice cloning and emotional speech synthesis
howTo: Clone github.com/resemble-ai/DramaBox and install its requirements
Download the ResembleAI/Dramabox weights from Hugging Face
Provide a reference voice WAV plus a prompt describing the line and delivery
Run src/inference.py to synthesize the audio to an output file
For repeated runs, start the warm TTSServer instead of cold-loading each time

example.label: Synthesize with a reference voice
example.content: python src/inference.py --voice-sample reference.wav --prompt 'A woman speaks warmly, "Hello, how are you today?"' --output output.wav

goodToKnow: Outputs are watermarked by default; cloning real people's voices without consent is unethical and often illegal.
Voice-reference denoising needs extra deps; without them it still runs but skips denoising.

llm/diffbot-small-xl.tagline: Open LLM grounded in a live knowledge graph
llm/diffbot-small-xl.overview: diffbot-small-xl is Diffbot's open-weight language model, fine-tuned from Llama and wired to Diffbot's knowledge graph and web tools so it answers from real-time facts instead of only memorized training data. It runs as a self-hosted server using vLLM and exposes an OpenAI-compatible API. Because it retrieves facts, it is aimed at reducing hallucinations on questions about real entities and current information.
capabilities: Answers using Diffbot's knowledge graph and real-time web retrieval
Fine-tuned from Llama, so it behaves like a familiar chat model
Self-hosted via a provided Docker image running vLLM
Exposes an OpenAI-compatible API for easy client integration
Designed to cite and ground facts to cut down on hallucinations
useCases: Developers needing an LLM that answers factual, up-to-date entity questions
Builders of research or knowledge tools who want grounded responses
Students comparing retrieval-grounded answers against a plain LLM
howTo: Pull the image: docker pull diffbot/diffbot-llm-inference:latest
Run it with GPU access, mapping port 8001 and setting the model via VLLM_OPTIONS
Wait for vLLM to finish downloading weights and report it is ready
Point the OpenAI Python client at your local base URL
Send chat requests; the server fetches facts from the knowledge graph as needed

example.label: Run the server
example.content: docker run --runtime nvidia --gpus all -p 8001:8001 --ipc=host -e VLLM_OPTIONS="--model diffbot/Llama-3.3-Diffbot-Small-XL-2412 --served-model-name diffbot-small-xl --quantization fp8 --tensor-parallel-size 2" diffbot/diffbot-llm-inference:latest

goodToKnow: The XL model uses fp8 quantization and tensor parallelism, so it expects a multi-GPU NVIDIA setup.
First start is slow because model weights download from Hugging Face automatically.

llm/hunyuan-vision-1.5-thinking.tagline: Vision model that reasons step by step
llm/hunyuan-vision-1.5-thinking.overview: Hunyuan Vision 1.5 (thinking mode) is Tencent's vision-language model that reasons step by step over images and text, working through a problem before answering rather than replying instantly. The thinking variant is aimed at harder visual tasks like chart reading, diagram interpretation, and multi-step visual questions. Note the weights are closed, so you typically access it through Tencent's API or hosted endpoints rather than downloading it.
capabilities: Combines image and text understanding in one vision-language model
Thinking mode reasons through multiple steps before answering
Targets harder tasks like charts, diagrams, and complex visual questions
Handles document and image understanding alongside free-form questions
Accessed via Tencent's hosted API rather than local weights
useCases: Analysts asking detailed questions about charts, tables, or diagrams in an image
Students who need an image explained with the reasoning shown
Developers building visual QA where step-by-step accuracy matters
howTo: Open the repo at github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanVision for API and access details
Obtain access credentials for Tencent's Hunyuan Vision API
Send a request containing your image plus a question, selecting thinking mode
Read the model's reasoning trace and final answer from the response
Tune your prompt to ask for the specific visual detail you need

example.label: Visual question
example.content: image (a bar chart) + "Which quarter had the largest drop, and by how much? Explain your reasoning."

goodToKnow: Weights are closed, so you cannot run this fully offline like the open models here.
Thinking mode is more accurate on hard tasks but uses more tokens and is slower than a direct answer.

llm/lfm2-5-230m-built-to-run-anywhere.tagline: Tiny 230M language model for phones and edge
llm/lfm2-5-230m-built-to-run-anywhere.overview: LFM2.5-230M is Liquid AI's open-weights language model with just 230M parameters, small enough to run on phones and edge devices instead of a server. It is designed for on-device use where latency, privacy, and offline operation matter. Despite its tiny size, it targets practical tasks like short-form generation, classification, and extraction at the edge.
capabilities: Runs locally on phones and edge hardware without a cloud server
Tiny 230M footprint keeps memory and battery use low
Handles everyday language tasks like short generation, classification, and extraction
Open weights you can download and embed in an app
useCases: Mobile developers adding offline AI features that protect user privacy
Students experimenting with LLMs on a laptop or phone without a GPU
Edge/IoT builders needing a small model that fits constrained devices
howTo: Read the announcement at liquid.ai/blog/lfm2-5-230m for model details and links
Download the LFM2.5-230M open weights from Liquid AI's model hub listing
Convert or load it with an edge runtime (such as llama.cpp or a mobile runtime)
Run inference locally on your device and send it short prompts
Benchmark on your target hardware to confirm latency and memory fit

example.label: Edge-friendly task
example.content: "Classify this message as spam or not spam: 'You won a free prize, click here.'"

goodToKnow: At 230M parameters it is far less capable than large models; keep tasks narrow and well-defined.
It shines on-device for privacy and offline use, not for complex multi-step reasoning.

llm/mistral-ocr-4.tagline: Document AI that reads PDFs and scans cleanly
llm/mistral-ocr-4.overview: Mistral OCR 4 is Mistral AI's document-understanding model that reads scanned pages, PDFs, and images and pulls out clean text, tables, and layout structure. Rather than just dumping raw characters, it preserves document structure so the output is usable downstream, for example as Markdown. It is offered through Mistral's API as a document-processing endpoint.
capabilities: Extracts text from scanned pages, PDFs, and images
Preserves structure like tables and layout, not just plain characters

useCases: Students who want a conversational model for questions and writing
Anyone doing chat-style text-and-image work
howTo: Sign in at OpenAI's platform and get an API key
Select the gpt-5-chat model
Send your conversational prompt, with images if needed
Read the reply and continue the conversation

example.label: Example chat prompt
example.code:
Model: gpt-5-chat
Prompt: "Help me write and refine a short story."

goodToKnow: Closed-weight, run on OpenAI's servers

llm/gpt-5-high.tagline: GPT-5 at high reasoning for hard problems
llm/gpt-5-high.overview: This is OpenAI's GPT-5 at its high reasoning setting, a closed text-and-image model that spends more effort on hard problems for stronger answers. The extra effort helps on tough, multi-step work. It's used through OpenAI's platform.
capabilities: Runs GPT-5 at high reasoning effort
Spends more effort on hard problems
useCases: Students tackling hard, multi-step text or image problems
Anyone needing stronger answers than a fast model gives
howTo: Sign in at OpenAI's platform and get an API key
Select gpt-5 with a high reasoning setting
Send your hard problem as a prompt
Read the response and refine as needed

example.label: Example API-style request
example.code:
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-5","reasoning":{"effort":"high"},"input":"Solve this step by step."}'

goodToKnow: Closed-weight, run on OpenAI's servers
High reasoning can be slower and cost more than lighter settings

llm/gpt-5-medium.tagline: OpenAI model tuned for coding and reasoning
llm/gpt-5-medium.overview: OpenAI's GPT-5 at its medium reasoning setting, a closed model strong at coding and technical tasks with balanced speed and depth. It is a closed model, so you reach it through OpenAI's API or hosted tools rather than downloading the weights. In everyday terms, students use it for writing and understanding code, plus reasoning and general chat.
capabilities: Strong at writing and explaining code
Works for general chat and writing too
useCases: Students stuck on a bug or trying to understand a code snippet
Learners who want technical explanations plus working code examples

example.label: Call it with the OpenAI Python SDK
example.code:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()
resp = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-5-medium",
    input="Explain photosynthesis to a 10-year-old."
)
print(resp.output_text)

howTo: Create an OpenAI account and get an API key from the developer console.
Store your API key as an environment variable so your code can read it securely.
Install OpenAI's official SDK (or use plain HTTP requests) in your project.
Send a request naming the model "gpt-5-medium" with your prompt, then read the response.
goodToKnow: This is a paid, closed model: you need an OpenAI account and API key, and usage is billed per token.
